strings.d1.s0.name: São Bento Station
strings.d1.s0.tips: A station hall covered in 20,000 azulejo tiles telling Portuguese history.
strings.d1.s1.name: Ribeira
strings.d1.s1.tips: UNESCO-listed riverside quarter of colourful houses; take in Praça da Ribeira and the narrow lanes.
strings.d1.s2.name: Dom Luís I Bridge
strings.d1.s2.tips: Double-deck iron bridge by a student of Eiffel; walk across the upper level (next to the metro).
strings.d1.s3.name: Taylor's Port Cellars
strings.d1.s3.tips: A port wine cellar in Gaia dating from 1692; audio tour with 3 tastings and a garden terrace.
strings.d1.s4.name: Jardim do Morro Sunset
strings.d1.s4.tips: Garden at the bridge end; watch the Porto skyline at sunset, then take the cable car (6 EUR) down.
strings.d1.b0.name: Graham's Port Lodge
strings.d1.b0.tips: Vintage port and river views; an alternative to Taylor's.
strings.d1.b1.name: Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar
strings.d1.b1.tips: Terrace of a round monastery on the Gaia hilltop; the best view.
strings.d2.s0.name: Livraria Lello
strings.d2.s0.tips: Often called the world's most beautiful bookshop (red staircase); book an online ticket for the 09:00 opening slot (the price counts towards a book).
strings.d2.s1.name: Clérigos Tower
strings.d2.s1.tips: A 76 m Baroque tower with 240 steps; panoramic city views.
strings.d2.s2.name: Igreja do Carmo
strings.d2.s2.tips: Twin churches with a blue-tiled side façade; look for the 1 m-wide house between them.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mercado do Bolhão
strings.d2.s3.tips: Restored 1914 market; cheese, tinned sardines and stalls on the upper floor.
strings.d2.s4.name: Café Majestic
strings.d2.s4.tips: A 1921 Belle Époque café on Santa Catarina; pricey but worth seeing.
strings.d2.b0.name: Casa Guedes Praça Poveiros
strings.d2.b0.tips: Pernil (roast pork leg) sandwich with Serra cheese; expect a queue.
strings.d2.b1.name: Igreja de São Francisco
strings.d2.b1.tips: Baroque interior covered in gold leaf (300 kg of gold); also catacombs.
strings.d3.s0.name: Pinhão Railway Station
strings.d3.s0.tips: The Linha do Douro train from São Bento takes 2.5 hours (along the river, sit on the right-hand side); the station is decorated with tiles.
strings.d3.s1.name: Quinta do Bomfim
strings.d3.s1.tips: Dow's vineyard; terrace tasting and a walk through the vines.
strings.d3.s2.name: Pinhão Rabelo Boat Tour
strings.d3.s2.tips: One hour on a traditional rabelo boat; the terraced vineyards are UNESCO-listed.
strings.d3.s3.name: Pinhão Lunch at Veladouro
strings.d3.s3.tips: Riverside tavern; try posta (veal steak) and Douro wine.
strings.d3.s4.name: Miradouro de Casal de Loivos
strings.d3.s4.tips: The best view of the valley (10 minutes by taxi); the return train leaves at 17:20.
strings.d3.b0.name: Quinta das Carvalhas
strings.d3.b0.tips: Vineyard on the opposite bank; jeep tour.
strings.d3.b1.name: Museu do Douro, Peso da Régua
strings.d3.b1.tips: On the way back, get off at Régua to visit the museum, then catch a later train.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tram 1 Ribeira–Foz
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 1930s wooden tram runs along the river to the Atlantic; board at the Infante stop.
strings.d4.s1.name: Foz do Douro Lighthouse
strings.d4.s1.tips: Lighthouse and crashing waves; see the Pérgola seafront columns.
strings.d4.s2.name: Praia dos Ingleses and Seafront
strings.d4.s2.tips: Winter Atlantic waves; stop for a coffee.
strings.d4.s3.name: Casa de Pasto da Palmeira Foz
strings.d4.s3.tips: Small plates facing the sea; modern Portuguese cooking.
strings.d4.s4.name: Palácio de Cristal Gardens
strings.d4.s4.tips: Terraced gardens with peacocks; views of the river and bridge. Take bus 500.
strings.d4.b0.name: Serralves Museum
strings.d4.b0.tips: Siza's contemporary art museum and Art Deco villa park; an alternative to the Crystal Palace.
strings.d4.b1.name: Brasão Cervejaria Foz
strings.d4.b1.tips: Francesinha (Porto's "heart attack" sandwich) with its sauce.
strings.d5.s0.name: Guimarães Castle
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1 hour by train; a 10th-century castle known as the "birthplace of Portugal".
strings.d5.s1.name: Palace of the Dukes of Braganza
strings.d5.s1.tips: Burgundian-style ducal palace; look out for the tapestries.
strings.d5.s2.name: Largo da Oliveira, Guimarães
strings.d5.s2.tips: UNESCO-listed medieval square; lunch at Cor de Tangerina.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bom Jesus do Monte
strings.d5.s3.tips: Take a bus or train to Braga; a Baroque zigzag staircase of 577 steps and a water-powered funicular (1882), with views.
strings.d5.s4.name: Braga Cathedral
strings.d5.s4.tips: Portugal's oldest cathedral; then the train back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Santuário do Sameiro
strings.d5.b1.name: Frigideiras do Cantinho Braga
strings.d5.b1.tips: A café dating from 1796; try the frigideira pastry.
strings.d6.s0.name: Aveiro Moliceiro Boat
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1 hour by train; canal boats in the "Venice of Portugal" (45 minutes) and Art Nouveau houses.
strings.d6.s1.name: Ovos Moles Confeitaria Peixinho
strings.d6.s1.tips: A pastry shop from 1856; ovos moles, an egg yolk sweet (shell-shaped).
strings.d6.s2.name: Costa Nova Striped Houses
strings.d6.s2.tips: 30 minutes by bus; candy-striped fishermen's houses (palheiros) and a beach.
strings.d6.s3.name: Costa Nova Lunch at Dóri
strings.d6.s3.tips: Lagoon-side fish restaurant; try the caldeirada (fish stew).
strings.d6.s4.name: Praia da Costa Nova
strings.d6.b0.name: Fábrica Vista Alegre
strings.d6.b1.name: Salpoente Aveiro
strings.d6.b1.tips: Bacalhau tasting menu in a former salt warehouse.
strings.d7.s0.name: Rua de Miguel Bombarda Galleries
strings.d7.s0.tips: A street of art galleries; Centro Comercial Bombarda for design.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cedofeita Neighbourhood
strings.d7.s2.name: Manteigaria Porto
strings.d7.s2.tips: Warm pastel de nata; near Clérigos.
strings.d7.s3.name: Rua das Flores
strings.d7.s3.tips: Pedestrian street; say goodbye at Casa Portuguesa do Pastel de Bacalhau.
strings.d7.s4.name: Trindade Metro Airport
strings.d7.b0.name: Bonjardim Grill
strings.d7.b0.tips: Piri piri chicken at a no-frills street restaurant.
strings.d7.b1.name: Casa da Música
strings.d7.b1.tips: Koolhaas's white concrete concert hall; tour at 11:00, an alternative to the galleries.
strings.note0: The Andante 24-hour pass costs 7 EUR (metro and bus); metro line E reaches the airport in 30 minutes. Book CP trains to the Douro, Guimarães and Aveiro online (sit on the right for the Douro). The hills are steep.
strings.note1: Winters are rainy at 10-15°C (Porto is wet); September to October brings the golden Douro grape harvest, Christmas lights go up on Aliados, and April to May is ideal.
strings.note2: Francesinha 12-15 EUR, pastel 1.30 EUR, port tasting 20-25 EUR, Lello 10 EUR (counts towards a book), coffee 1 EUR; round up the bill as a tip.
strings.note3: Book Lello online for 09:00; visit Clérigos in the morning; the Douro train fills up on summer weekends, so book ahead; Bolhão market is closed.
strings.note4: Tripas à moda do Porto (tripe, hence the city's nickname "tripeiros"), bacalhau, francesinha, vinho verde, tawny and ruby port.
strings.note5: Ribeira is safe at night; the Gaia cellars close at 17:00.
strings.transit.name: Andante 24-hour pass
strings.transit.why_chosen: Metro, bus and tram; includes metro line E to the airport
